public_rationale: The accessible reporting provides a concrete example of hardware arriving before deployment. It does not establish that at least $200 billion of NVIDIA GPU sales preceded installation by a year. Neither the existence of warehoused equipment nor aggregate capital spending supplies the missing sale-to-installation reconciliation. The evidence also does not establish a sufficiently comprehensive upper bound to contradict the claim.
limitations: The usable deployment report is secondary reporting on internal emails.
Complete rack purchases are not equivalent to NVIDIA GPU sales.
The cumulative sales period is inferred from the surrounding passage.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: At least $200 billion, possibly over $300 billion, of NVIDIA's GPU sales were made a year or more ahead of installation.

statement.excerpt: It’s very clear that at least $200 billion — if not more than $300 billion — of NVIDIA’s GPU sales have been made a year or years in advance, just as the company telegraphs it will make over $670 billion in revenue in its fiscal year 2028 (starting February 2027).

from_speaker: made a year or years in advance
our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion makes installation into operational infrastructure the reference point for 'in advance'.
The firm commitment is at least $200 billion. More than $300 billion is a tentative extension.
The contextual buildout begins in 2022. I assess sales from January 1, 2022 through publication on September 22, 2026.
Sales means completed GPU sales valued at NVIDIA's sale proceeds, not purchase commitments, customer rack costs or annualized revenue.
The accounting basis is estimate because the passage presents the speaker's inferred allocation of sales and capital expenditures.
The reference to fiscal 2028 revenue is background, not a separate forecast in this claim.
criteria.support_condition: Matched sales and commissioning records establish at least $200 billion of NVIDIA GPU sales in the stated cohort with at least twelve months between sale and operational installation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comprehensive matched records, or a reliable upper bound covering the relevant sales cohort, establish that less than $200 billion qualifies.

evidence.explanation: This secondary account of Business Insider's August-email reporting describes equipment received before deployment. It does not establish twelve-month delays, GPU-only NVIDIA sale proceeds, or the $200 billion threshold.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A reconciled dataset or independently verified investigation matching NVIDIA GPU sale proceeds and dates to customer installation dates, sufficient to establish a total above or below $200 billion.
